Hi Marta / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the thoughtful demo last week. One open item that came up internally on your side was how our billing "smoothing" or crediting would apply for the type of intermittent streaming traffic you described (short bursts of many small streaming calls followed by long quiet periods).

Quick background on their actual pattern: occasional telemetry jobs that stream ~4-8k tokens per job, 10–30 jobs in a burst, then nothing for many hours. They were worried about minimums and whether they would be charged for a full session/context bucket on every tiny burst.

Could you confirm the following so we can propose a concrete crediting example to share with procurement?
- Do you consider a "job" here to be a single streaming request or a multi-request session?
- Are you looking for a flat monthly credit, or a usage-based smoothing mechanism that reduces per-burst peaks?
- Any procurement constraints (e.g., minimum commit, PO timing) we should bake into the proposal.

I can follow up with a worked example from our side once you confirm; we'd like to avoid surprise overage charges for the first quarter.

Hi Marta — thanks for the details. I wanted to give a concrete explanation and sample math so procurement can see how this would look on an invoice. I'll keep it short and example-driven.

Background on our smoothing proposal (pilot-friendly):
- We offer a transient smoothing pool that aggregates token usage spikes over a rolling 72-hour window. Tokens consumed above the customer's normal baseline are first drawn from the pool before being billed at regular unit rates.
- The pool size for pilots is defined as a % of your 30-day median daily token usages (we typically start pilots at 25% of median daily usage). The pool decays daily (unused credits reduce by a simple linear factor over 3 days).
- Importantly for streaming jobs: we measure chargeable units at the token granularity, not per-session buckets. Minimums (session-flooring) apply only when requests exceed a configured context-length threshold AND the request is kept open for >120s. Short-lived streaming calls that are under that threshold do not automatically get a full-context minimum applied.

Worked example you asked for (25 jobs x 6,000 tokens each in one burst = 150,000 tokens):
- Baseline: your 30-day median daily tokens = 80,000 tokens. Pilot smoothing pool = 25% * 80,000 = 20,000 tokens.
- Burst consumption = 150,000 tokens. Pool covers 20,000 tokens. Remaining billable = 130,000 tokens.
- Because each streaming job is <120s and context length <32k tokens, no per-session minimums are applied; charges are token-based.
- Invoice line example:
  - Smoothing credit applied: -20,000 tokens @ list rate (credit shown as a negative line item)
  - Billable tokens this period: 130,000 tokens @ your negotiated token rate

Alternative (if you want a stronger protection): we can add a short-term burst cap where any single burst above X tokens is billed at a capped effective rate up to Y tokens per 24h; that requires a short commit (30–90 days) to be economical.

I've attached our smoothing-policy-v1.pdf which has the legal-friendly wording and the decay schedule. Rishi — flagged you because I expect legal/procurement will ask about how this interacts with committed usage and rollovers.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the invoice layout.

Best,
